props.title: Kids
props.initialSlug: Raw teen drama exposes NYC youth's dark reality

sections.content: Kids (1995) hit audiences like a sledgehammer, exposing the raw underbelly of 90s youth culture through its unflinching portrayal of NYC teenagers. Larry Clark and Harmony Korine's controversial debut follows 24 hours of casual sex, drug use, and violence among Manhattan skaters. The film's documentary-style realism, achieved by casting actual street kids like Leo Fitzpatrick and Chloë Sevigny, created immediate scandal. But beyond the shock value, Kids captured a specific moment of pre-internet teenage wasteland and AIDS crisis anxiety that influenced everything from Thirteen (2003) to Mid90s (2018).

sections.content: The cultural impact of Kids spawned a wave of unflinching youth-focused films in the late 90s and 2000s. Bully (2001) continued Larry Clark's exploration of teenage amorality, while films like Ken Park (2002) and Spring Breakers (2012) pushed boundaries even further. The documentary approach influenced international cinema too, with La Haine (1995) examining Parisian youth culture and This Is England (2006) capturing British skinhead subculture through a similar lens of teenage alienation.

Beyond just shock value, these films tapped into genuine teenage experiences often sanitized by mainstream cinema. While American Teen (2008) took a documentary approach to high school life, fiction films like The Basketball Diaries (1995) and Another Day in Paradise (1998) continued exploring youth counterculture through a grittier lens. The lasting influence of Kids can be seen in recent coming-of-age films like We Are Who We Are (2020) and Red Rocket (2021), which maintain that raw authenticity while examining contemporary youth culture. SUBHEAD: Evolution of Youth Culture on Film

sections.content: The DNA of Kids runs through later explorations of teenage life like The Florida Project (2017) and American Honey (2016), which maintain that documentary-adjacent style while examining youth in poverty. Even mainstream teen films began incorporating grittier elements, as seen in Cruel Intentions (1999) and Alpha Dog (2006). The film's influence extends to international cinema with works like Fish Tank (2009) and Girlhood (2014) offering raw portraits of teenage life in Britain and France respectively.
